research_concepts: role transferability across contexts (portability after a move)
methodological_questions: Can a portability test of cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shapers reach useful power with 24 units?
How should cut and drive shares be measured from play-by-play and how reliable are those labels?
What sample and power are needed to compare role transfer between shaper types?
Does the prior connector-portability result carry over to this question and data?

historical_evidence.finding: Cut- vs drive-based connector portability. Pre-move cut share predicted whether a connector's organizational function reproduced after a move (Cut share rho=+0.265, p=0.011, AUC 0.653; Cut-drive rho=+0.314, p=0.002; Drive rho=-0.278, p=0.007). Top cut tercile 65% portable (median Delta +0.167) vs bottom 35% (median -0.039). LOO AUC 0.622; permutation p=0.005. Sample n=92 connector movers. Recorded limitation: LIM:small_sample, RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Connector diet x destination structural-gap match. Binary match rate 15.7%. CONNECTOR taxonomy delta match vs mismatch p=0.156 with n=5/14; travel-check delta p=0.413; all-movers binary delta p=0.0283 but Spearman(match_score, delta)=-0.034 p=0. Recorded as not the licensed connector test. Sample n=19 taxonomy connectors, n=198 all movers.

DRIVE-as-BEST counter vs constrained mix. Observed gap -0.066 PPP (p=0.2175 vs B_fixed); MDE at 80% power ~0.180 PPP (SD~0.34). Recorded as A_unanswerable; n=44 cannot distinguish a true null from an effect up to 0.18 PPP. Validation status: no_validation_recorded.

Destination outcome (net rating) checks for movers (archive). Recorded as 'underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality' with no numbers. Dropped from Paper 1. Sample not recorded. Failure type A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Binary diet-match test of connector portability against destination structural gaps, including an all-movers analysis.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with LIM:small_sample. Connector subsets were n=19/40. The all-movers binary p=0.0283 did not replicate as a continuous Spearman (rho=-0.034), so it was not the licensed test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparison of observed DRIVE-based H2 PPP against a feasibility-constrained baseline.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with LIM:low_power_large_MDE and LIM:small_sample. Observed gap -0.066 was below the MDE of 0.180 at n=44, so a true null could not be separated from a sizable effect.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Destination on-court net-rating change for movers as a portability outcome.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with LIM:low_power_large_MDE and LIM:small_sample. Stated underpowered and null after correcting for landing-spot quality; numbers not recorded, so the basis cannot be audited.

evidence_establishes: A prior project study (FAM:SF-CHT-057, recorded as supported) reported a positive association between pre-move cut share and connector portability in n=92 movers, with a permutation check and LOO AUC.
Earlier attempts on closely related portability questions with small samples (n=19 to n=44) were recorded as untestable because power was too low for the effect sizes involved.
The project has recorded that small-sample and large-MDE limitations are the dominant failure mode for this family of questions.
evidence_does_not_establish: That cut-heavy shapers' roles transfer better in the present question. The retrieved positive result is for connector movers in a different unit set (n=92), and the present data has 24 units.
Whether the positive SF-CHT-057 result replicates in 2022-23 to 2025-26 data. The record does not describe replication, and its outcome measure is not confirmed to match the present one.
Any effect size for the current question; no numeric result for a cut-heavy versus drive-heavy comparison in 24 units was retrieved.
The reliability of the cut/drive labels or of the Delta outcome under the current data sources.
own_inferences: With 24 units, a two-group comparison of portability can detect only very large differences. The retrieved MDEs (about 0.18 PPP at n=44) suggest the present design would be far less powered.
SF-CHT-057 used 92 movers, so its 65% versus 35% tercile contrast is not evidence for a 24-unit design. Using it as a prior would overstate the expected effect.

The positive SF-CHT-057 result, with a weak LOO AUC (0.622) and reliance on a 5000-shuffle permutation test, is the sort of result that inflates under selection and needs a clean replication before reuse.

Because the question's outcome and predictor both come from play-by-play, label and outcome dependence (cut/drive shares and any role measure derived from the same possessions) could generate spurious association.
uncertainties: The unit of analysis for n=24 is not stated (team, player, or player-season); the power calculation depends on it.
The portability outcome and its operational definition for the present data are not specified in the task statement.
Retrieval returned no numeric detail for SF-PAP-029 (sample size and effect not recorded), so its evidential weight cannot be assessed.
The 2025-26 playoffs were complete as of 2026-06-21, but the regular season and playoff data for earlier seasons may have changed in the source feed; data version was not verified.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved record set shows that three closely related portability or counter-factual tests with n=19 to n=44 were recorded as untestable because power was too low. This makes the 24-unit version of the present question very unlikely to reach useful power, so I moved from a proceed-with-changes plan to do_not_proceed as posed. The one positive record (SF-CHT-057, n=92) was not used as confirmation; at most it motivates a pre-registered replication in a larger unit set.

blocking_constraints.text: With 24 units, the MDE for a cut-versus-drive portability contrast is expected to be far larger than any plausible effect; comparable designs at n=44 had MDE 0.18 PPP and were recorded as untestable.
Cut and drive shares and the portability outcome have not been shown to be reliable at the unit level in the present data.
Per-unit possession counts for play-type shares may be too sparse to estimate cut and drive proportions stably, especially for players with few moves.

prior_work.summary: A closely related question (pre-move cut share vs connector portability) was reported as supported in n=92 movers (SF-CHT-057). Three related tests with smaller samples were recorded as untestable (SF-APPS-090, SF-APPS-024, SF-PAP-029) because of low power. The present question, with 24 units, has not been answered, and the retrieved evidence does not show a usable test at that sample size.

risks.text: 24 units give very low power; retrieved comparable designs at n=44 had MDE 0.18 PPP and were recorded as untestable.
Cut/drive shares and the portability outcome need test-retest or split-half reliability before use.
If the portability outcome is derived from the same play-by-play as the cut/drive shares, shared construction can create spurious association.
Movers may be selected on prior performance, so pre-move shares and post-move outcomes can both reflect regression to the mean.
Position, usage, team pace and landing-spot quality can confound the cut-share association; SF-PAP-029 was null only after landing-spot correction.
SF-CHT-057 reports several metrics (cut share, cut-drive, drive, terciles, AUC); selecting the best one inflates the apparent effect.
The permutation check in SF-CHT-057 used label shuffles; placebo outcomes (e.g. non-mover stability) were not recorded as tested.
Play-type usage and roster construction change across 2022-23 to 2025-26; a shaper-type label may mean different things in different seasons.
Play-type initiation labels from the graph database may be misassigned, and the mapping of play types to cut versus drive is not verified.

methodological_questions: can role transferability be tested with n=24 units
how to measure cut-heavy versus drive-heavy play style from play-by-play
sample size and power for comparing role stability between shaper types
reliability and derived labels from play-type possession records
args.query: Do cut-heavy shapers' structural roles transfer across contexts better than drive-heavy shapers? Prior studies of play-type initiation, role stability, and small-sample team-level role analyses in NBA play-by-play data.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
